meteo.sourcesTitre: Where this data comes from and how to read it
meteo.pluiePersistante: It is raining, and it is set to last.
meteo.accalmieVers: A dry spell is forecast around {{heure}}.
meteo.pluieProchainesHeures: Rain is forecast in the next few hours.

meteo.nowcastExpire: The 15-minute forecast has expired: the latest reading is too old to say anything about the next two hours.
meteo.nowcastHorsZone: No 15-minute forecast for this area — it falls outside the fine-mesh models. Only the hourly probabilities are reliable here.

eclairage.lampadaires: Street lights: lights recorded in OpenStreetMap, or synced from city open data. One light = one glow on the map.
eclairage.ruesEclairees: Lit streets: streets tagged as lit in OpenStreetMap. Not every road carries that information, which is why we infer lighting for some roads from nearby street lights or from an adjacent lit street.
eclairage.avertissement: An area without a glow is not necessarily unlit: more often than not, the data is simply missing. Few French cities publish an open dataset of street lights, and OpenStreetMap is not complete everywhere, especially in rural areas.
eclairage.aucunLampadaire: No street lights synced for this area.
eclairage.couverture: OpenStreetMap covers the whole area; city open datasets exist only for some cities, and densify the coverage there.
eclairage.lampadairesMobile: The street lamps themselves (OpenStreetMap and open data from metropolitan areas) are not shown on mobile: there are too many of them for the phone’s memory. They are still used to infer the lit streets above, and remain visible on the web version.
eclairage.avertissementMobile: A street that is not highlighted is not necessarily unlit: most of the time, the data is simply missing. Few French cities publish an open dataset of street lamps, and OpenStreetMap is not complete everywhere, especially in rural areas.

meteoModal.releve: The reading is taken at a single point in the centre of the urban area, and the banner carries the highest alert level of the moment. It is a regional level: a storm cell is 5 to 15 km across and we only sample one point. Hence “Storm risk”, never “Storm on your route”.
meteoModal.avertissement: So we speak of a storm risk, never of a storm on your route. The weather does not change the calculated route: it informs you, it does not send you on a detour based on a forecast of this resolution.
meteoModal.pluie30Texte: The 15-minute forecast comes from the fine-mesh models AROME (Météo-France) and ICON-D2 (DWD). Outside their coverage it is not shown at all, rather than being silently interpolated from the hourly forecast.
meteoModal.sourcesTexte: Forecasts: Open-Meteo (DWD ICON-D2, Météo-France AROME, NOAA GFS).
meteoModal.ventPonts: Wind adjusts the displayed duration of the route, never the route itself. Below 3 °C, bridges of at least 30 m are flagged: a deck loses heat from both faces and freezes one to two hours before the nearby roadway.

airModal.cellulesTexte: The index shown is the European Air Quality Index (EAQI), computed by the European Copernicus service (CAMS). Each coloured cell covers about {{resolution}} km across: this is a regional level
airModal.cellulesAvertissement: At this resolution, two neighbouring streets share the same index. For route calculation, when regional air quality worsens, the algorithm relies on an exposure indicator inferred from the road network to favour the streets furthest from traffic.
airModal.pastillesTexte: The dots are real measuring stations. A model such as CAMS can lag behind a sudden, local event; a station measures the air with no delay. When a nearby station records a peak, the route takes it into account even if the cells stay calm.
airModal.pastillesAvertissement: Two scales: cells in EAQI (European), dots in US AQI — the sensors' native scale, not converted.
airModal.sourcesTexte: Cells: CAMS ENSEMBLE, redistributed by Open-Meteo (forecast up to 24 h). Dots: World Air Quality Index Project (waqi.info).
